elements.name: External Production Credential Boundary
elements.description: Production Neo4j and embedding-provider credentials are supplied to the Node.js application only through approved secure external configuration. Approved Neo4j configuration names are ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_URL, ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_USERNAME, and ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_PASSWORD; legacy ARGO_NEO4J_URI, ARGO_NEO4J_USERNAME, and ARGO_NEO4J_PASSWORD aliases are not authorized as substitutes or overrides. Runtime neo4jUri may be materialized only from approved ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_URL, and runtime embeddingCredential may be materialized only from approved QWEN_KEY after provenance checks; neither runtime field is a separately authorized external key, fallback, default, literal, command-line value, or graph/Cypher value. Secret keys QWEN_KEY and ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_PASSWORD may originate only from direct process environment variables or the unique local file .argo/.env when that file is ignored, untracked, regular, non-reparse, and access-restricted. Process environment has precedence; if both sources define a key with different values, startup fails closed rather than silently overriding or falling back. Secrets are never hardcoded, defaulted, accepted from another file or command line, transported through Cypher text or parameters, or emitted to stdout/stderr, errors, logs, graph evidence, runner records, snapshots, or artifacts.

views.description: ArchiMate-inspired motivation viewpoint for framing stakeholder concerns before modeling solution details. Stakeholders: business partners, business managers, requirements owners, enterprise architects, and acceptors. Concerns: architecture mission, drivers for change, assessments, high-level goals, desired outcomes, value, principles, and hard constraints. Purpose: designing, deciding, and informing. Scope: motivation and strategy context. Use this view to answer who cares, why the change matters, what success means, and which constraints cannot be violated. Typical elements: Stakeholder, Driver, Assessment, Goal, Outcome, Value, Meaning, Principle, Requirement, Constraint, Course of Action. Do not place implementation components here unless they are needed only as evidence for a stakeholder concern.

ArchiMate-inspired strategy viewpoint combining Strategy, Capability Map, Value Stream, and Outcome Realization concerns. Stakeholders: business managers, product owners, enterprise architects, business architects, and portfolio decision-makers. Concerns: business-oriented results, capability boundaries, value streams, resources, investment focus, and capability-to-outcome coverage. Purpose: designing and deciding. Scope: strategy with links to motivation and core elements when needed. Use this view to answer what business outcomes are in scope, which capabilities create or support them, and where value is produced. Typical elements: Outcome, Capability, Value Stream, Resource, Course of Action, Product, Value, Meaning, and selectively core elements that realize outcomes. Do not decompose detailed workflows or technical implementation here.

ArchiMate-inspired business behavior viewpoint drawing from Organization, Product, and Business Process Cooperation viewpoints. Stakeholders: process owners, domain experts, operational managers, business analysts, and product managers. Concerns: responsibilities, authority, business process dependencies, business services, product composition, contracts, shared information, and observable business events. Purpose: designing, deciding, and informing. Scope: mainly Business layer, with application links only when they explain business process support. Use this view to answer how the business works, who performs behavior, what events trigger it, what business objects are used, and what services or products are exposed. Typical elements: Business Actor, Business Role, Business Collaboration, Business Process, Business Function, Business Interaction, Business Event, Business Service, Business Object, Contract, Product, Representation. Do not turn this view into an application structure or code module map.

ArchiMate-inspired realization and usage viewpoint combining Requirements Realization, Application Usage, Service Realization, Application Cooperation, and Implementation and Deployment concerns. Stakeholders: enterprise architects, application architects, solution architects, process architects, and implementation designers. Concerns: how requirements, capabilities, business processes, and business services are realized by application services, components, data objects, and supporting technology; consistency, completeness, dependency visibility, and service orchestration. Purpose: designing and deciding. Scope: multiple layers and multiple aspects, but only along business-to-system realization paths. Use this view to answer how a business capability is carried by system responsibilities and which application or technology elements are relevant to that realization. Typical elements: Requirement, Constraint, Capability, Business Service, Business Process, Application Service, Application Component, Application Interface, Application Function or Process, Data Object, Technology Service, Node, Artifact. Do not include low-level implementation detail unless it changes a business-visible responsibility or dependency.

ArchiMate-inspired implementation and migration viewpoint extended with ARGO acceptance semantics. Stakeholders: business acceptors, project managers, operational managers, enterprise architects, delivery owners, and downstream agents. Concerns: acceptance control points, observation points, risk, work package scope, deliverables, plateaus, gaps, migration order, cross-cutting concerns, and consistency between delivery dependencies and architecture dependencies. Purpose: deciding and informing, with enough design detail to plan delivery. Scope: implementation and migration plus explicit business acceptance semantics. Use this view to answer how the change will be accepted, what must be observed, which work packages or plateaus are involved, what depends on what, and what risks could invalidate delivery. Typical elements: Goal, Outcome, Requirement, Constraint, Work Package, Deliverable, Implementation Event, Plateau, Gap, Business Actor, Business Role, and core elements affected by delivery. Do not use this view as a backlog dump; every item must affect acceptance, sequencing, or risk.

Top-level baseline architecture map governed by five universal business viewpoints. It follows the ArchiMate viewpoint mechanism: select content by stakeholder concerns, purpose, and scope, not by layer folders. The five child viewpoints provide the default AI navigation path from stakeholder intent to outcomes and capabilities, business behavior, capability realization, and acceptance-delivery sequencing. ArchiMate layers remain implicit in element types and may be used by validators or specialized sub-views, but they are not the default modeling entry point.

views.view_name: Native Technology and Embedding Release Requirements
views.description: Viewpoint: Requirements Realization Viewpoint; Concern: production runtime boundary, approved secret-source isolation, canonical harness environment loading, neo4jUri and embeddingCredential resolution, canonical Neo4j configuration names, explicit embedding qualification, real-provider evidence, and canonical authority are release requirements before index delivery; Purpose: designing, deciding, and handoff preparation; Scope: Node.js/Neo4j production mainline, Argo harness initialization through node .argo/scripts/ensureArgoHarnessEnvironment.js, native retrieval, the human-approved Alibaba Cloud Model Studio OpenAI-compatible provider profile, qualification-2026-07-25 with acknowledged alias drift, explicit dimensions 1024, opt-in live E2E through a controlled Neo4j instance, direct-process or unique ignored/untracked .argo/.env sourcing with fail-closed conflict and Windows ACL preflight, approved provider secret QWEN_KEY as the only source for runtime embeddingCredential, approved Neo4j names ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_URL/USERNAME/PASSWORD with ARGO_NEO4J_DATABASE_URL as the only source for runtime neo4jUri, rejection of legacy ARGO_NEO4J_URI/USERNAME/PASSWORD aliases, and canonical graph authority; Rationale: this Requirements Realization view traces configuration and credential constraints to the existing runtime and native retrieval realization path, permits only the approved local secret-file/process sources without weakening zero-leakage evidence, requires canonical Neo4j names plus neo4jUri and embeddingCredential resolution before projection, provider, database, or index side effects, requires live evidence without treating offline fakes as delivery proof, and preserves TS-09 adapter/lifecycle work outside this handoff.

Viewpoint: Technology Usage Viewpoint; Concern: application-to-provider and vector-projection dependencies, batching scalability, secure credentials, runtime coupling, TS-09 adapter generation/persistence proof, and partial-failure isolation; Purpose: designing, deciding, and handoff preparation; Scope: canonical mutation through affected-record extraction, independent provider invocation, productionGraphRagRuntime.generateAffectedEmbeddings() outcome evidence, and versioned Neo4j vector persistence; Rationale: this view isolates the production embedding-generation path and now makes TS-09 an explicit blocking W3 gate so DT-05, DT-16, and DT-17 scoped evidence cannot be mistaken for full W3 acceptance.

Viewpoint: Implementation and Migration Viewpoint; Concern: W3 accepted lifecycle evidence must be integrated into the actual mutation write success path so a single applySystemArchitectureMutation call automatically triggers live approved Qwen embedding, Neo4j vector persistence/queryability, and failure-state release gates before downstream semantic seed work relies on it; Purpose: deciding and handoff preparation; Scope: W3 to W3.1 to W4 delivery sequencing, actual touched-id extraction from mutation response, automatic embeddingLifecycle invocation, mutation response alignment semantics, vector index persistence, and semantic-query prohibition for unaligned states; Rationale: this view belongs under the acceptance-delivery anchor because it defines a supplemental integration work package, its corrected observable E2E acceptance boundary, and the downstream gate it imposes on W4 without weakening existing W3/TS-09 acceptance. Historical manual post-mutation lifecycle evidence is insufficient for W3.1 acceptance.

Viewpoint: Requirements Realization Viewpoint; Concern: requirements owners, ICT architects, operators, and acceptors need A-D to realize one fail-closed canonical semantic lifecycle while WP-P1 persistence/backfill and WP-P2 retrieval/readiness remain private; Purpose: designing; Scope: exact dual-gated init reconciliation, durable all-path incremental indexing, persistent readiness per query, sole public getSystemArchitecture surface, canonical authority, and external credential constraint; Rationale: this view is a Requirements Realization Viewpoint instance because it designs traceability from A-D to the application, data, and constraint elements that realize them and explicitly supersedes the former three-tool public journey.

Viewpoint: Application Usage Viewpoint; Concern: operators and application/process architects need one explicit safe path through argo init and getSystemArchitecture without separate public lifecycle choreography; Purpose: designing; Scope: operator invocation, structural projection, private full reconciliation, fail-closed readiness, sole query service, and gated plateau; Rationale: this Application Usage Viewpoint instance designs how canonical init uses private WP-P1/WP-P2 capabilities and how getSystemArchitecture serves reads. Both gates disabled is structural-only with zero vector effects; exact dual-enabled valid configuration reconciles; half-enabled or unsafe/missing configuration fails closed; no standalone lifecycle tools are public.
